artworks.title: Bellerophon and Stheneboea (Antioch mosaic)
artworks.description: Antioch Four Seasons mosaic: Stheneboea (Anteia) with Bellerophon — the queen whose false accusation sends the hero to Lycia, preserved in Roman pavement at Antakya.

artworks.title: Bellerophon and Stheneboea (mosaic detail)
artworks.description: A closer view of the same Antioch panel — Stheneboea and the hero who rejected her, the Proetid court intrigue as late-antique floor myth.

popCulture.creator: Homer
popCulture.description: Book VI — Homer's Anteia (Stheneboea) lusts for Bellerophon; rejected, she turns Proetus against him with a lying letter.

popCulture.title: Bibliotheca

popCulture.description: Apollodorus names Stheneboea as Proetus' wife whose false charge launches Bellerophon toward the Chimera.

popCulture.title: Stheneboea
popCulture.description: Wife of Proetus — Homer's Anteia — whose rejected desire and forged letter send Bellerophon to Lycia.
